article_sentences: Component II of the RELIEF (Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation) initiative will now remain in force until March 31, 2027, the Department of Commerce said on Monday.
The initiative is aimed at encouraging exporters to obtain insurance cover from the Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (ECGC) for eligible shipments to specified regions.

Under the scheme, eligible exporters can receive 95 per cent risk coverage, and protection against increases in insurance premiums beyond pre-disruption levels is available during the eligible period, the department said in a notification dated September 30.

The extension comes as continuing geopolitical tensions in West Asia disrupt maritime logistics across the Gulf and surrounding regions, raising freight costs, insurance premiums and war-related risks for Indian exporters.
What does the scheme cover?
Component II covers standalone and whole-turnover ECGC policies obtained on or after March 16, 2026.
Eligible cargo includes full container load (FCL), less than container load (LCL) and refrigerated containers, while energy shipments are excluded.
Exporters seeking benefits must submit claims and supporting documents through ECGC's customer portal.
The corporation has also published video tutorials on its official YouTube channel to guide exporters through registration and claim submission.

Launched on March 19, 2026, RELIEF is part of the government's Export Promotion Mission and is intended to help Indian exporters manage exceptional increases in logistics costs and export risks arising from disruptions along the Gulf and wider West Asian maritime corridor.
The extension is intended to sustain trade flows and reduce exporters' exposure to elevated shipping and insurance costs while geopolitical uncertainty persists.
Its impact will depend on the extent of eligible exporters' participation and the costs and risks covered under the scheme.

stories.headline: NDRF deploys nine teams in A.P. and Yanam for cyclone response
stories.title: NDRF deploys nine teams in A.P. and Yanam for cyclone response
stories.summary: Five teams kept in reserve; schools and colleges to remain closed on October 27 and 28
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) has deployed seven teams in Andhra Pradesh and two in Yanam to carry out rescue and relief operations during the cyclone, said NDRF 10th Battalion Commandant V.V.N. Prasanna Kumar.
Speaking to The Hindu on Monday, he said five teams had been kept in reserve and more would be deployed, if necessary, depending on the situation.
Instructions had been issued to coordinate with officials of the Disaster Management, Revenue and Police departments.
One team was on standby at the Regional Response Centre in Visakhapatnam, he said.
Beaches across the State have been closed, and the public has been advised against venturing near seashores and river bunds to take selfies.
Coastal patrolling has been intensified, and the Marine.
Police have been put on alert in view of the cyclone, officials said.
The State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) has also deployed eight teams at various locations across the State to assist with rescue and relief operations over the next three days.
Meanwhile, the Education Department has declared holidays for schools and colleges on October 27 and 28 in view of the forecast of heavy rain.
Eluru District Collector K. Vetriselvi said holidays had been declared for all schools and Anganwadi centres in the district.
In Krishna and NTR districts, holidays have been declared for all schools and colleges for the next two days.

article_sentences: The Real Time Governance Society (RTGS), Andhra Pradesh has asked people in Cyclone Arnab-affected areas of State to report emergencies and local problems through Mana Mitra WhatsApp Governance.
People can report power outages, fallen trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging and other cyclone-related issues by sending “Hi” to 9552300009 on WhatsApp.
To register a complaint, citizens must select “Arnab Cyclone Issues”, followed by “Report Issue” and “Confirm”.
They can then select “Registration”, enter their name, district and mandal, describe the problem and upload photographs, if available.
Registered grievances will be forwarded to the concerned local authorities for necessary action and early resolution.
RTGS has appealed to citizens to use the facility to report cyclone-related problems promptly and help authorities respond effectively.
Once registered, the grievance will be forwarded to the concerned local authorities for necessary action and early resolution, a release said.

stories.title: Between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam: Where Cyclone Arnab is expected to make landfall

article_sentences: Cyclone Arnab is approaching Andhra Pradesh with winds forecast to reach 140 kmph.
Authorities have activated disaster preparations, several states face heavy-rain warnings, and Indian Railways has cancelled eight trains and altered two others.

Hyderabad: Cyclone Arnab is moving towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, prompting authorities to issue alerts, prepare rescue teams and suspend several train services ahead of its expected landfall on Wednesday, October 28.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the cyclonic storm was located over the east-central and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal at 5.30 am on Monday.
It was around 650 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam and moving westwards at approximately 15 kmph.
The storm is forecast to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by Monday night and a very severe cyclonic storm on Tuesday.
According to the IMD forecast cited in the reports, it is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam.
The system could bring sustained winds of 115–125 kmph, with gusts reaching 140 kmph.
Authorities are preparing for possible flooding, power disruptions, damage to infrastructure and interruptions to transport services.
The Centre has stepped up preparedness in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Puducherry.
Authorities in other regions have also been asked to remain vigilant because of the possibility of heavy rainfall.
Cabinet Secretary T. V. Somanathan chaired a meeting of the National Crisis Management Committee to review preparations and coordinate response measures.

stories.headline: Tension in Kurnool as TDP supporters ‘disrupt’ YSRCP leader’s election campaign
stories.title: Tension in Kurnool as TDP supporters ‘disrupt’ YSRCP leader’s election campaign
stories.summary: YSRCP leaders allege some locals claiming to be TDP activists allegedly abused Hafeez Khan, obstructed the party’s election campaign, and threatened to cause harm to their leader and also those accompanying him
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Mild tension prevailed for some time in Kurnool city during election campaigning after some persons, allegedly affiliated with the TDP, tried to stop and attack former Kurnool MLA and YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) leader M.A. Hafeez Khan in the 16th ward on Monday.
Mr. Hafeez Khan visited the Vaddegiri locality in the 16thward to campaign for his party’s contesting candidate.

According to YSRCP leaders, some locals claiming to be TDP activists allegedly abused Mr. Hafeez Khan, obstructed the party’s election campaign, and threatened to cause harm to their leader and also those accompanying him.
Police immediately intervened and removed Mr. Hafeez Khan from the locality.
An infuriated Mr. Hafeez Khan got back into his car and challenged the alleged attackers, but the police convinced him to leave the place.
Mr. Hafeez Khan later lodged a complaint with the One Town police seeking action against those responsible for the incident.

Reacting sharply to the allegations made by the former MLA, Industries and Commerce Minister T.G. Bharath Gupta said that the YSRCP leaders were making false allegations against the NDA for political gain.

Addressing the media during his election campaign for NDA candidates in Kurnool on Monday, Mr. Bharath claimed the YSRCP leader could not handle the situation when the public questioned him during his campaign.
“Instead of responding to the public’s questions, he lashed out and began criticising the TDP leaders.
When the public asks questions, one should give answers, but lashing out at them is not appropriate,” he said.
He claimed the YSRCP leaders were resorting to criticism as they could not bear the growing popularity of the coalition government among the people.
“YSRCP leaders are responsible for the murders that have taken place in Kurnool over the last two years.

stories.headline: Over 61,000 Form-7 applications filed by election officials in Karnataka, none cites reason
stories.title: Over 61,000 Form-7 applications filed by election officials in Karnataka, none cites reason
stories.summary: Officials say they were instructed to file Form-7 applications for shifted, duplicate, underage, deceased and non-citizen voters, but auto-generated forms left the reason blank
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: At least 61,059 Form-7 applications seeking the deletion of names from Karnataka’s electoral rolls were filed by election officials themselves, with not a single application mentioning a reason for the deletion, a mandatory requirement under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.
Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and Assistant Electoral Registration.

Officers (AEROs), listed as the objectors in these applications, said the system “auto-generated” the forms with their digital signatures when voters could not be reached during hearings on notices issued for no mapping or logical discrepancies, and the voters were therefore marked as “ineligible”.
This meant the same election machinery was raising objections to voters’ names and deciding on whether they should remain on the rolls.
Under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 an objection that is not filed in the prescribed manner, including stating the reason, is liable to be rejected.
The officials said they had been instructed to file Form-7 applications if a voter had shifted, had a duplicate entry elsewhere, was underage, had died, or was not an Indian citizen.
But as the forms were auto-generated, the reason for seeking deletion was left blank.
With no reason recorded, neither the voter nor anyone examining the electoral roll can establish why a particular name was marked for deletion or verify whether the removal was justified.

Moreover, these categories of voters (ASDDO or Absent, Shifted, Duplicate, Dead and Others) had already been checked during the enumeration phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which led to more than 1.07 crore names being deleted from Karnataka’s draft electoral roll.
Most deletions were on the grounds of voters having permanently shifted, followed by those marked as absent.
The number of Form-7 applications filed by election officials rose sharply after the claims and objections period ended on September 23, 2026.
Between August 24 and September 23, only 192 such applications were received.

stories.headline: DAC clears proposals worth Rs 2.12 lakh crore for armed forces procurement
stories.title: DAC clears proposals worth Rs 2.12 lakh crore for armed forces procurement
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 26: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh on October 26, 2026, accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) i.e. in-principle administrative to various capital acquisition proposals of the Defence Forces at an estimated cost of about Rs 2,12,000 crore. For the Indian Army, approval was accorded for the procurement of High Mobility Vehicles (HMV), Self-Propelled Tracked Gun System, Gun Shot Response System (GSRS), Light Multi Role Helicopters (LMRH), Very Short-Range Air Defence System (VSHORADS), Platform Based Counter Unmanned Aerial System (C-UAS), Unmanned Aerial System Brick Long Range, Surveillance UAV, Integrated Surveillance and Strike System and Long Range Kamikaze Drone System. The HMVs will enhance operational capabilities, logistic support and mobility in challenging terrains. The Self-Propelled Tracked Gun System will provide matching mobility and firepower to mechanised formations. The GSRS will serve as a force multiplier providing real-time situational awareness of the forces. The LMRH will be used by both the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force for Reconnaissance and Surveillance, Combat, Search and Rescue of troops, Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief etc. The VSHORADS will engage new generation small size aerial threats, while C-UAS will enhance survivability of Tanks in the modern battlefield. The Surveillance and Drone Systems will enhance the surveillance and targeting capabilities of the Indian Army. For the Indian Navy, approval was given for the procurement of Active Offboard Decoy System (AODS) and other major Naval platforms. The AODS will enhance the credibility of anti-missiles defence, especially against modern anti-ship missiles of adversaries. The indigenously designed and constructed major Naval platforms will possess modern-day warfare capabilities and enhance the combat capability of the Navy. For the Indian Air Force, approval was accorded for the procurement of Helicopters, Air Defence Systems, Weapons and Mobile X-Band Doppler Weather Radar System to enhance the air defence and war fighting capabilities. The procurement of Special Utility Helicopters will help the Indian Air Force to meet the important air transport requirements. The X-Band Doppler Weather Radar System will provide high-resolution, localised weather surveillance in forward areas. Out of the total AoNs accorded, approximately 82% of the procurements will be made from the Indian Industry.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Quashes Karnataka Land Acquisition Over Fraud & Bribery In Housing Society Scheme, Orders Land Restoration To Owners
stories.title: Supreme Court Quashes Karnataka Land Acquisition Over Fraud & Bribery In Housing Society Scheme, Orders Land Restoration To Owners
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (October 26) set aside the land acquisition proceedings of a privately owned land for construction of a cooperative housing society in Bengaluru, after finding that the private players had lured the state government to approve the proposed extent of land for acquisition, and there was no approved housing scheme or layout plan before acquisition took place.
The Court also directed that possession of the acquired land be restored to the respective landowners, irrespective of whether they had challenged the acquisition.
The landowners must refund any compensation received from the government, without interest.
The Court clarified that this would not require them to refund amounts received in private transactions.
The bench enhanced the costs payable to each petitioner to ₹50,000.
It, however, deleted the direction to initiate contempt proceedings against government officers, considering the passage of time.
According to the Court, a mere approval of the proposed extent of land, without an approved housing scheme and layout plan, would not suffice for land acquisition.

“What is required is not just an approval of the extent and the mere expression of a laudable housing scheme, but housing sites demarcated for allotment to landless members with the detailed descriptive lay-out plan laid before the Government.

We find no such scheme having been laid out before the Government.”, observed a bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice K. Vinod Chandran, emphasising that the power of eminent domain, being a condemnation of a privately owned for public purpose can only be with authority of law, and presence of a public purpose.

stories.headline: Supreme Court refuses to ease bail condition for Delhi riots accused to attend law classes in Ghaziabad
stories.title: Supreme Court refuses to ease bail condition for Delhi riots accused to attend law classes in Ghaziabad
stories.summary: A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi declined to modify Shadab Ahmad’s bail condition requiring him to remain in Delhi during the trial, questioning why he hadn’t sought the change from the trial court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (October 26, 2026) refused to relax a bail condition barring Shadab Ahmad, an accused in the alleged larger conspiracy behind the 2020 Delhi riots, from leaving the national capital to attend law classes at a university in Ghaziabad.
A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi declined his plea to modify the condition requiring him to remain in Delhi during the trial.
“This we will not modify...
We know why you joined that law college, leaving out all the law colleges inside Delhi,” the Bench said.

On January 5, 2026, the Court had granted bail to Mr. Ahmad, along with activists Gulfisha Fatima, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohd Saleem Khan and Meeran Haider, in the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case, while imposing stringent conditions and cautioning that any misuse of liberty would invite cancellation of bail.

In the same ruling, the Court had denied bail to former JNU student leaders Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam, who had been incarcerated since 2020, while allowing them to seek bail afresh after the examination of protected witnesses, or after a year.

Counsel for Mr. Ahmad told the Court that he was on the “path of reformation” and had secured admission to a law course in Ghaziabad, after failing to gain admission to the three-year LL.B. programme at Delhi University.
“He is on the path of reformation, my Lords.
He has secured admission in a law college...
He applied for a three-year course in Delhi University, but he was not able to secure admission there.
He will go in the morning and come back in the evening...
It is 10 km from Delhi,” the counsel submitted.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Warns Rajasthan Of CBI Probe Into Regularisation Of Illegal Mining Along Jojari-Luni-Bandi River System
stories.title: Supreme Court Warns Rajasthan Of CBI Probe Into Regularisation Of Illegal Mining Along Jojari-Luni-Bandi River System
stories.summary: “Making 20 lakh people live in hell cannot be compared with your economic viability of a few thousand people,” Justice Mehta remarked.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: “Making 20 lakh people live in hell cannot be compared with your economic viability of a few thousand people,” Justice Mehta remarked.

The Supreme Court on Monday (October 26) warned that it may order a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into alleged illegal mining and the regularisation of mining areas along the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system in Rajasthan, questioning why State authorities had granted mining leases in areas where illegal mining had been detected, and regularising illegal leases.

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta cautioned that several officials could face serious consequences if the State failed to take corrective action, while expressing concern over the authorities' failure to protect the rivers despite repeated judicial directions.
“What have you done about providing the statistics of the mining, illegal mining in the rivers?
What have you done?
You have regularized.
You know, Mr. Raju, when illegal mining was pointed out, your officers went ahead and regularized those leases.
We feel that if you don't pull up your socks and don't mend your ways, we'll be compelled to direct a CBI investigation.
That would land many of your officers in hot waters,” Justice Mehta told Additional Solicitor General SV Raju, appearing for Rajasthan.

The Court was hearing the Supreme Court's suo motu proceedings concerning pollution in the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system, which has affected the environment and the lives of approximately 20 lakh people.

In August, the Court directed that no construction or development activity shall be permitted within 100 metres of the edge of the river system until completion of a scientific exercise to determine and demarcate the High Flood Line and the requisite ecological buffer zones, as an interim measure to protect the river ecosystem from further ecological degradation.

Today, the Court questioned the State's explanation that it had registered hundreds of cases relating to illegal mining, observing that registration of cases did not address the fact that mining areas previously identified as illegal had subsequently been regularised.
